inspection_summary: Inspected all 2,426 normalized lines of this 49-page survey. The mathematical text runs from the foundational function-space form of Voronin universality through Euler-product, joint, strong, mixed, recurrence, weighted, discrete, character-aspect, hybrid, quantitative, composite, and ergodic variants, followed by references. The extraction breaks some displayed formulas across lines, but the checked surrounding prose makes every selected mechanism recoverable; units that depend on exact inequalities or hypotheses retain explicit formula-risk notes.

sections_inspected.label: Front matter, abstract, and contents
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bibliographic orientation and a complete map of the survey; no standalone semantic unit.

sections_inspected.label: 1. Voronin’s universality theorem
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines the approximation property, states its modern positive-density form, and identifies analytic, Diophantine, and probabilistic proof architectures.

sections_inspected.label: 2. A rough sketch of the history
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Organizes the subject into three research stages and records how the problem focus moved from variants to class extension and newer composite or ergodic directions.

sections_inspected.label: 3. Generalization to zeta and L-functions with Euler products
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Explains how Euler products, coefficient mean estimates, positive density, and prime-geodesic input control which L-function families and strips are universal.

sections_inspected.label: 4. Joint universality for zeta and L-functions with Euler products
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Develops simultaneous approximation and translates functional independence into orthogonality, rank, and prime-coefficient conditions.

sections_inspected.label: 5. Strong universality
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Removes the nonvanishing target restriction for non-Euler-product series, derives zero-density consequences, and tests how broad such universality can be.

sections_inspected.label: 6. Joint strong universality
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Compares matrix and logarithmic-independence hypotheses and exposes algebraic relations as genuine obstructions to simultaneous approximation.

sections_inspected.label: 7. Universality for multiple zeta-functions
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Transfers strong universality to multiple sums and links the result to a lower-depth zero-free condition.

sections_inspected.label: 8. Mixed universality
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Combines Euler-product and non-Euler-product functions through independence of their two exponent systems.

sections_inspected.label: 9. Strong recurrence
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Relates self-approximation to the Riemann hypothesis and records parameter-dependent successes, gaps, and almost-periodic analogies.

sections_inspected.label: 10. Weighted universality
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Replaces ordinary shift density by weighted sampling under a weighted ergodic-average condition.

sections_inspected.label: 11. Discrete universality
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Studies approximation along arithmetic progressions of shifts and the resonances imposed by the step size.

sections_inspected.label: 12. Chi-universality
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Moves the varying parameter from vertical shift to character or discriminant and derives value- and class-number density consequences.

sections_inspected.label: 13. Other applications
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Derives derivative density and functional or differential independence from universality.

sections_inspected.label: 14. General notion of universality
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Places zeta universality inside a topological orbit framework and connects it to rearrangement and Kronecker-Weyl universality.

sections_inspected.label: 15. Hybrid universality
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Couples function approximation to finite phase constraints and uses the coupling to control combinations and polynomials of L-functions.

sections_inspected.label: 16. Quantitative results
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Identifies ineffectivity in the classical proof and surveys replacements that bound approximation density and first occurrence.

sections_inspected.label: 17. Universality for derived functions
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Asks which operators preserve universality and supplies continuity, preimage, and analytic mechanisms for composite functions.

sections_inspected.label: 18. Ergodicity and universality
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Recasts universality as recurrence of dynamical or random orbits and states an equivalence with ergodic universality.

sections_inspected.label: References and author address
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bibliographic support only; inspected and excluded from semantic unit selection.

accepted_units.title: Voronin universality as positive-density function-space approximation
accepted_units.why_material: The source passes from a single-disc approximation to the modern compact-set, positive-lower-density theorem and then isolates its two basic engines: mean approximation by finite Euler products and Kronecker-Weyl control of prime phases.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the definitions of the function spaces and strip needed to interpret the theorem without reconstruction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Displayed formulas are line-broken but readable with the surrounding prose; retain the compact-set, nonvanishing-target, and positive-density hypotheses.

accepted_units.title: Three proof routes and their distinct approximation inputs
accepted_units.why_material: Contrasts Voronin's Hilbert-space rearrangement route, Good and Gonek's modification, and Bagchi's probabilistic route, while identifying Mergelyan approximation as shared infrastructure for the latter approaches.
accepted_units.context_note: Follows the proof skeleton in u01 and supplies method-level alternatives rather than another theorem statement.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-dominant; theorem names and attributions are clear in extraction.

accepted_units.title: From value denseness to functional probability laws
accepted_units.why_material: The survey reframes Voronin universality as an infinite-dimensional extension of value denseness and explains Bagchi's lift of Bohr-Jessen weak convergence from C to a function space.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes derivative denseness, the function-space interpretation, and why functional limit theorems become a reusable proof route.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The probability-measure display is recoverable from prose; exact normalization should be checked against the source lines.

accepted_units.title: Three-stage evolution of universality research
accepted_units.why_material: Records that the early period already generated most major variants, the middle period broadened the class of functions, and the recent period introduced mixed, composite, and ergodic directions; this distinguishes conceptual branching from mere chronology.
accepted_units.context_note: The publication-history details support why certain early results remained inaccessible and later schools expanded them.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-only.

accepted_units.title: Euler products suggest universality, but mean-value control fixes the strip
accepted_units.why_material: Shows that an Euler product motivates transfer beyond zeta but does not suffice: available mean-value estimates restrict Dedekind zeta universality, and coefficient hypotheses delimit general periodic or Euler-product classes.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes representative families and the explicit explanation of the narrower Dedekind strip.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several series and condition (3.1) are formula-sensitive; the causal point is stated clearly in prose.

accepted_units.title: Positive density replaces unavailable first-moment coefficient information
accepted_units.why_material: Identifies the obstacle for automorphic L-functions—lack of the needed prime-coefficient absolute-sum asymptotic—and repairs it by combining the ordinary prime sum with a known squared-coefficient asymptotic.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the resulting unconditional cusp-form theorem and the extension to wider axiomatic classes.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Coefficient normalizations and equations (3.2)-(3.3) are extraction-sensitive; use the checked prose for the replacement mechanism and verify formulas from the retained original if instantiated.

accepted_units.title: Higher moments can remove a pointwise Ramanujan-type hypothesis
accepted_units.why_material: Tracks how universality transfers to elliptic, Hecke, Rankin-Selberg, and Maass L-functions, and highlights Nagoshi's removal of a Ramanujan assumption by invoking a fourth-power coefficient mean.
accepted_units.context_note: The many families are retained because they demonstrate which analytic inputs substitute for unavailable pointwise bounds.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-dominant; coefficient notation is mildly degraded but the assumption-removal logic is explicit.

accepted_units.title: Prime geodesics play the prime-number-theorem role for Selberg zeta
accepted_units.why_material: Transfers the universality mechanism from arithmetic primes to primitive geodesic data and makes the error exponent in the prime geodesic theorem determine the attainable strip.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the conjectural improvement and the claimed widest possible region.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The Pell and prime-geodesic displays are formula-dependent; conceptual dependence on the exponent alpha is prose-supported.

accepted_units.title: Joint universality requires an independence mechanism
accepted_units.why_material: Defines simultaneous approximation by a common shift and explains why orthogonality of distinct Dirichlet characters embodies the independence required for joint universality.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the full target setup and the foundational joint theorem.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The multi-target density display is fragmented but semantically recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Matrix rank as a reusable finite-dimensional independence certificate
accepted_units.why_material: Unifies several joint-universality results by translating primewise coefficient behavior into full row rank of a matrix, with periodic zeta-functions as a concrete realization.
accepted_units.context_note: Keeps enough setup to identify what rows, columns, and prime classes represent.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Matrix indices and periodic-sequence notation are formula-sensitive but legible.

accepted_units.title: Prime-coefficient orthogonality as the expected joint-universality criterion
accepted_units.why_material: Links twisted automorphic joint universality to a prime number theorem in progressions and then motivates Selberg's conjectural orthogonality criterion, while retaining the footnoted warning that a naive iff form has counterexamples.
accepted_units.context_note: The caution at lines 596-601 is integral: pairwise coefficient cancellation alone is not presented as settled sufficiency.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equations (4.2)-(4.3) are extraction-sensitive; the conjecture and counterexample warning are clear.

accepted_units.title: Fourier-coefficient orthogonality removes disjoint-strip separation
accepted_units.why_material: Shows the progression from a weaker two-function approximation on disjoint strips to full joint universality and identifies coefficient orthogonality, rather than periodicity, as the decisive new input.
accepted_units.context_note: Overlaps u11 to preserve the weaker precursor and the conjectural context against which Mishou's theorem is assessed.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The approximation display is broken across lines; theorem cases and method summary are prose-supported.

accepted_units.title: Strong universality removes the nonvanishing target barrier
accepted_units.why_material: Contrasts Euler-product universality with Hurwitz strong universality, explains how transcendental and rational parameters invoke different independence reductions, and isolates the still-open algebraic-irrational case.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the theorem statement so the meaning of strong is grounded in the changed target class.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Hurwitz-series and character-decomposition formulas are line-broken; parameter cases and target distinction are explicit.

accepted_units.title: Strong universality forces linearly many zeros
accepted_units.why_material: Uses a target with one zero and Rouche's theorem to turn positive-density approximation into a linear lower bound for zeros in every substrip.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the local disk construction and the zero-counting corollary.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: One zero-count notation has an apparent T/t OCR mismatch, but the proof mechanism is fully recoverable from prose.

accepted_units.title: A non-Euler-product general Dirichlet series criterion for strong universality
accepted_units.why_material: Moves from examples to a six-condition theorem using rationally independent exponents, continuation, growth, mean square, exponent counting, and coefficient energy.
accepted_units.context_note: The preceding Estermann, Lerch, and periodic examples motivate why a general theorem is useful.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Conditions (i)-(vi) are recoverable but symbol-heavy; verify exact exponents and normalizations from the original before reuse.

accepted_units.title: Analytic continuation alone is too weak to predict universality
accepted_units.why_material: States the broad Linnik-Ibragimov expectation and immediately falsifies its naive formulation with a sparse Dirichlet series collapsing to a simple rational function.
accepted_units.context_note: The counterexample identifies missing coefficient richness as a live requirement rather than silently repairing the conjecture.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Sparse-series formula is mildly degraded but its support on powers of two and closed form are explicit.

accepted_units.title: Joint strong universality shifts from matrix rank to exponent independence
accepted_units.why_material: Compares early matrix-rank hypotheses for Lerch or periodic Hurwitz systems with a later criterion based directly on linear independence of all logarithmic exponents.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the correction that transcendence must be strengthened to algebraic independence in the earlier theorem.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Matrix entries and the logarithmic set are formula-sensitive but checked.

accepted_units.title: Arithmetic and measure-theoretic routes enlarge admissible parameter families
accepted_units.why_material: Shows that algebraic dependence between transcendental parameters need not obstruct joint universality, extends to arbitrary real twists under stronger alpha assumptions, and gives an almost-everywhere twist result with explicit full-measure subfamilies.
accepted_units.context_note: Ends with Mishou's conjecture to mark the remaining unproved parameter-wide claim.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Parameter families are symbol-dense but prose and theorem boundaries are recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Functional relations can destroy joint universality
accepted_units.why_material: Explains why no naive joint analogue of broad single-series universality is available: inversion formulas and bounded-sequence constructions impose relations and non-denseness.
accepted_units.context_note: Preserves both positive and negative outcomes for generalized Lerch series rather than treating independence as only a sufficient-condition problem.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Definitions (6.3)-(6.4) are extraction-sensitive; the obstruction claim is clear in prose.

accepted_units.title: Disjoint translated domains manufacture joint universality from one orbit
accepted_units.why_material: Provides a simple reusable construction: translate one universal function over disjoint compact sets so a single approximation problem encodes several target functions.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the strong-universality variant.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose and elementary notation are clear.

accepted_units.title: Multiple-zeta universality depends on a lower-depth zero-free value
accepted_units.why_material: For Euler-Zagier-Hurwitz multiple sums, treats the first variable as the approximation variable and makes nonvanishing of the remaining lower-depth zeta value an explicit condition for strong universality.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the Barnes motivation and the exact theorem hypotheses.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Nested multiple sums are visually degraded; the theorem's variable roles and zero-free condition are prose-readable.

accepted_units.title: Mixed universality unifies prime and shifted-integer exponent systems
accepted_units.why_material: Combines an Euler-product zeta target with a strong Hurwitz target and identifies linear independence of the union of prime logarithms and shifted-integer logarithms as the essential proof input.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes periodic and multi-family extensions to show how the bridge generalizes.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The joint approximation display is fragmented; target nonvanishing asymmetry and independence set are clear.

accepted_units.title: Riemann hypothesis as strong recurrence of zeta
accepted_units.why_material: First uses known zero density to rule out strong universality for zeta, then shows that RH permits zeta itself as a nonvanishing target and records Bagchi's converse, yielding an iff self-approximation criterion.
accepted_units.context_note: The distinction between impossible strong universality and conditional strong recurrence is essential.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The self-approximation display is readable despite line breaks.

accepted_units.title: Scaled self-approximation from logarithmic independence
accepted_units.why_material: Connects recurrence to almost periodicity and derives joint approximations at algebraically independent shift scales using Baker-type independence of prime logarithms.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the special two-scale self-approximation and notes that d=0 recovers the RH-equivalent case.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The multi-scale display is fragmented; parameter conditions are explicit.

accepted_units.title: Rational-scale recurrence has exceptional resonances and repaired proof gaps
accepted_units.why_material: Separates the all-irrational result from rational cases, records that two published all-rational arguments had a gap, gives the repaired range, and contrasts zeta with log-zeta self-approximation.
accepted_units.context_note: This is valuable negative evidence: failure of an argument is not silently converted into a theorem.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The exceptional condition on the reduced fraction is clear; exact displayed inequalities should be retained.

accepted_units.title: Weighted universality follows from weighted ergodic averaging
accepted_units.why_material: Replaces uniform sampling of shifts by a weight and shows that a weighted analogue of Birkhoff-Khinchin is the condition that transports Bagchi's proof.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes bounded-variation and divergence assumptions so the weighted theorem is not detached from its admissibility conditions.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Integral normalizations and the o-bound are formula-sensitive but recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Sampling on an arithmetic progression introduces arithmetic resonance
accepted_units.why_material: Defines discrete universality via positive density among integer shifts and demonstrates across examples that the arithmetic nature of the step h affects whether phase equidistribution survives.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes Reich's baseline theorem and contrasting rationality conditions from later families.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The discrete density display is clear; some exponential conditions are prose-stated.

accepted_units.title: Some coefficient structure removes step-size restrictions
accepted_units.why_material: Records an elliptic/newform universality result valid for every nonzero step and a general Dirichlet-series theorem where algebraic exponents and rational exponential step data suffice.
accepted_units.context_note: Contrasts directly with the conditional examples in u27.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Strip and exponential hypotheses are clear.

accepted_units.title: Discrete mixed universality modifies Euler factors to match the step
accepted_units.why_material: When the discrete step resonates rationally, removes exactly the Euler factors at primes dividing the associated numerator or denominator; alternative full independence restores the unmodified zeta result.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the source's correction that the cited theorem's argument proves the modified-L statement, not the printed unmodified one.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The Euler product and joint displays are fragmented; the set of removed primes and correction are explicit.

accepted_units.title: Character-aspect universality replaces vertical shifts by a family parameter
accepted_units.why_material: Reframes universality as positive-density approximation while Dirichlet characters vary with modulus, and records the restricted modulus families for which the proof is valid.
accepted_units.context_note: The footnote correction on permissible modulus sets is included in the next unit's span only as nearby support; this unit retains the theorem's explicit alternatives.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The character-count normalization is formula-sensitive but readable.

accepted_units.title: Discriminant-aspect universality respects real symmetry and yields arithmetic density
accepted_units.why_material: Shows how varying real characters changes the target geometry—positive values on the real axis—and turns functional density into density statements for L-values and quadratic class-number expressions.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes prime-discriminant, RH-equivalence, and Hecke-character extensions as the boundary of the aspect method.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Class-number expressions are line-broken; the symmetry and positivity restrictions are clear.

accepted_units.title: Universality implies derivative density and functional independence
accepted_units.why_material: Derives finite-dimensional density of zeta and its derivatives from function-space universality, then uses it to exclude any nontrivial continuous-coefficient relation and hence algebraic differential equations.
accepted_units.context_note: Keeps the full relation form and its specialization to polynomial coefficients.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equation (13.1) is extraction-sensitive but its quantification and consequence are prose-supported.

accepted_units.title: Universality as rearrangement and orbit density
accepted_units.why_material: Connects Fekete and Birkhoff universal functions to Riemann rearrangement and Pecherskii's Hilbert-space analogue, then packages Voronin's theorem as density of a translation orbit relative to a target subset.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the topological definition and its explicit instantiation for zeta.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: One power-series display is fragmented; the topological mapping definition is clear.

accepted_units.title: Kronecker-Weyl is joint universality on a torus
accepted_units.why_material: Expresses joint universality abstractly as density in a product space and realizes rational independence as density of a phase orbit on a torus, unifying the Diophantine and zeta meanings of universality.
accepted_units.context_note: Sets up the hybrid construction of the next section.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Mapping superscripts and exponentials are mildly displaced but interpretable.

accepted_units.title: Hybrid universality couples functional targets with phase constraints
accepted_units.why_material: States simultaneous approximation of several L-functions together with prescribed prime phases and then broadens the phase condition to arbitrary rationally independent frequencies.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the direct synthesis of the two orbit pictures in u33-u34.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The max/sup and phase inequality display is formula-sensitive; prose names both coupled components.

accepted_units.title: Hybrid universality makes linear combinations strongly universal
accepted_units.why_material: Explains how controlling phases handles products or coefficients and yields strong universality, hence linearly many zeros, for nontrivial Dirichlet-series-weighted linear combinations of jointly hybrid-universal L-functions.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes Dedekind products and Dirichlet-polynomial applications as motivation for the general theorem.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The linear form is broken at a page line but recoverable; nonvanishing hypotheses on coefficients must be preserved.

accepted_units.title: Polynomial closure propagates zero-density consequences to many zeta families
accepted_units.why_material: Extends the linear-combination mechanism to polynomials with Dirichlet-series coefficients and explains why this yields off-critical-line zero lower bounds for several otherwise diverse zeta constructions.
accepted_units.context_note: The family list is retained as evidence of transfer breadth, not as separate mechanisms.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-only apart from generic polynomial notation.

accepted_units.title: Ineffective rearrangement blocks quantitative universality
accepted_units.why_material: Defines density and first-hit quantitative questions, identifies Pecherskii rearrangement as the source of ineffectivity, and shows Good's replacement by convexity and quantitative equidistribution.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the log-zeta to zeta exponentiation bridge.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Definitions of density and first hit are line-broken; method comparison is explicit.

accepted_units.title: Explicit bounds are possible but extremely weak
accepted_units.why_material: Provides a concrete small-disc lower bound for approximation density and double-exponential upper bound for first occurrence, then records functional-limit-speed and Taylor/derivative routes to other quantitative statements.
accepted_units.context_note: The extreme bound sizes are conceptually important evidence about effectivization difficulty.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Numerical constants and exponents are readable but should be verified from the source if used computationally.

accepted_units.title: A preimage-plus-continuity condition lifts universality through operators
accepted_units.why_material: Frames composite universality for operators on holomorphic function spaces and gives a Lipschitz-type criterion combining nonvanishing preimages of polynomial targets with local stability.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes derived examples such as derivatives, powers, exponentials, and sine to show the criterion's semantic reach.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The operator inequality and inverse-image condition are symbol-heavy but recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Analytic composites can be handled through differential-equation lifting
accepted_units.why_material: Contrasts broad family extensions of the operator method with an alternative approach that uses weak approximation, the implicit function theorem, and Picard-Lindelof theory for analytic functions of zeta and its derivatives.
accepted_units.context_note: Preserves the small-circle limitation of the alternative result.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The multivariable function notation is clear; prose carries the method and limitation.

accepted_units.title: Universality is dense recurrence of a translation orbit
accepted_units.why_material: Defines joint ergodic universality for iterates of a measure-preserving transformation and states its equivalence to ordinary target approximation, with positive-density recurrence along almost every orbit.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes both ordinary and strong target classes and the ergodic-system definition.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Iteration notation and density display are fragmented; quantified roles are clear.

accepted_units.title: Random walks and Brownian motion can generate universal orbits
accepted_units.why_material: Extends deterministic vertical translation to random lattice paths and uses the result to motivate a dynamical-systems view of universality and the RH recurrence criterion.
accepted_units.context_note: The final RH interpretation is presented as a research viewpoint, not as proof evidence.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The almost-sure density formula is readable; lattice side conditions are only referenced, so the unit does not claim their exact form.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: A layered architecture for universality proofs
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Across classical, probabilistic, positive-density, and quantitative routes, a reusable architecture separates analytic approximation of the function, controllability or equidistribution of phases, and a density or recurrence argument; the main variants replace one layer without discarding the others.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This is a within-survey synthesis, not a theorem that every cited universality proof factors uniquely into these layers.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Independence is representation-dependent
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The independence needed for simultaneous approximation appears as character orthogonality, matrix rank, prime-coefficient correlation, logarithmic independence, or removal of resonant Euler factors depending on the chosen representation and sampling scheme.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The listed conditions mix sufficient, conjectural, and corrected criteria and must not be collapsed into one established equivalence.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: The nonvanishing target condition marks an Euler-product divide
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Ordinary zeta universality approximates nonvanishing targets, whereas strong universality for non-Euler-product series admits zeros and thereby forces many zeros; for zeta itself, the compatible substitute is self-recurrence, whose validity is equivalent to RH.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The survey does not prove that having or lacking an Euler product alone is a necessary-and-sufficient criterion for strong universality.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Relations are as informative as independence
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Sparse support, inversion identities, resonant step sizes, and exceptional rational scalings show that universality can fail or require repair when the orbit is trapped by an algebraic or arithmetic relation.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Some boundaries remain incomplete, and a failed or repaired proof is not evidence that all excluded cases are false.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Universality transports through constructions when control survives
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Disjoint shifts, derivatives, hybrid phase control, linear or polynomial combinations, and stable operators generate new universal functions when target preimages and approximation errors can still be controlled.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Each transport has its own hypotheses; the survey provides no unrestricted closure principle for arbitrary transformations.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Universality, recurrence, and dynamics are one orbit seen at different resolutions
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Value distribution, function-space approximation, weighted sampling, self-recurrence, torus density, ergodic iteration, and random-walk sampling all study how an orbit visits target neighborhoods under different state spaces and clocks.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The final dynamical interpretation of RH is explicitly heuristic motivation beyond Bagchi's precise recurrence equivalence.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Analytic input quantitatively determines where and how universality is visible
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Mean-value regions, coefficient moments, prime-geodesic errors, lower-depth zero-free values, and effectiveness of approximation tools control the admissible strip, assumptions, or observable density rather than merely polishing a fixed universality statement.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: These dependencies come from heterogeneous theorems and do not yield a single formula predicting every universality region.
